data.definition: APT-like AgentOS-native manager that installs, verifies, activates, rolls back and explains capability packs, semantic tools, policies, model profiles, workflow packs, runtime adapters, guest images, test packs and trust metadata.

data.title: Traditional package manager replacement in first wave
data.rationale: AgentOS may wrap apt/dpkg/rpm later, but the ecosystem manager must first manage AgentOS-native contracts and safe activation metadata rather than raw host package mutation.

data.definition: The controlled transition from verified staged artifact to effective runtime behavior, always mediated by policy, capability, audit and rollback gates.

data.description: Stable manifest and registry schemas for AgentOS-native artifact kinds.
Offline-capable APT-like manager for search, verify, stage, activate, rollback and explain flows.
Trust tiers, channels, signatures, provenance, SBOM, revocation and advisory flow for Production Distro.
Proposed home for ArtifactManifest, RegistrySnapshot, ActivationPlan and ActivationReport contracts.

data.insight: First shippable ecosystem slice should be local registry plus policy/workflow/test packs, not public marketplace or remote package channels.

data.definition: Human-readable and machine-lockable identifier agentos:<kind>/<publisher>/<name>@<version> bound to digest, publisher identity and registry snapshot hash.

data.imports: Activation must be typed semantic operation rather than maintainer script
data.formatting: All production artifact activation requires signed metadata and replay evidence

data.insight: Every ecosystem activation needs local-only replay, adversarial fixtures, rollback drill and provenance hashes before Production Distro promotion.
